title: test: test_mod_io_device event test missing volatile on TEST_PROTECT flags — stale handler risk
description:
## What is wrong
test_mod_io_device.c:126-168 — the 'publishes relay_changed event'
test uses TEST_PROTECT() (setjmp/longjmp) but declares its cleanup
flags without volatile:

  bool handler_registered = false;  // NOT volatile
  bool mod_io_ready = false;        // NOT volatile

  if (TEST_PROTECT()) {
      ...
      mod_io_ready = true;       // modified inside setjmp scope
      ...
      handler_registered = true;  // modified inside setjmp scope
  }

  if (handler_registered) {   // indeterminate after longjmp
      esp_event_handler_instance_unregister(...);
  }

C11 7.13.2.1p3: variables of automatic storage duration modified
between setjmp and longjmp that are not volatile-qualified have
indeterminate values. If an assertion fails inside TEST_PROTECT,
longjmp restores pre-modification register values, so
handler_registered may remain false. The event handler is never
unregistered, leaving it pointing at the now-returned stack frame's
capture struct. A later event delivery writes to freed stack
memory — corruption or crash.

Both test_device_config_device.c and test_rest_api_device.c correctly
use `volatile bool fixture_captured` for the same pattern.

## Fix
  volatile bool handler_registered = false;
  volatile bool mod_io_ready = false;
close_reason: Completed

title: firmware: partition table has zero spare bytes — no headroom for flash geometry variance
description:
## What is wrong
firmware/partitions.csv layout:
  nvs:      0x9000  size 0x4000  → ends 0xD000
  otadata:  0xD000  size 0x2000  → ends 0xF000
  phy_init: 0xF000  size 0x1000  → ends 0x10000
  coredump: 0x10000 size 0x10000 → ends 0x20000
  ota_0:    0x20000 size 0x1F0000 → ends 0x210000
  ota_1:    0x210000 size 0x1F0000 → ends 0x400000

ota_1 ends at exactly 0x400000 (4MB). Zero spare bytes.

The plan (Step 1) says: 'Size OTA slots from the real firmware binary
with explicit headroom, instead of assuming a vague ~1.9MB budget.'
The original plan layout left 0x1E000 (120KB) spare.

Also, NVS shrank from the plan's 0x6000 (24KB) to 0x4000 (16KB).
ESP-IDF recommends >= 0x6000 for NVS to ensure adequate flash wear
leveling across pages. Smaller NVS reduces the effective write
endurance.

## Fix
Shrink OTA slots slightly to restore spare bytes. The plan's
0x1E0000 (~1.875MB) per slot would leave 0x1E000 (120KB) spare.
Restore NVS to 0x6000 (24KB) per the plan.
close_reason: Completed

title: firmware: default event loop created inside rest_api_start instead of main.c boot sequence
description:
## What is wrong
rest_api_start() in rest_api.c:285 calls esp_event_loop_create_default()
internally. The plan (Step 9) specifies event_loop_create as the second
step of the boot sequence in main.c, before any component init.

Currently this works because device_config_init() and board_init()
don't need the event loop. But when network_init() is added (Step 5),
it will need the event loop to register IP_EVENT_ETH_GOT_IP handlers
BEFORE rest_api_start is called.

The plan's boot sequence:
  nvs_flash_init -> event_loop_create -> device_config_init ->
  board_init -> ... -> network_init -> ... -> rest_api_start

Current main.c:
  device_config_init -> board_init -> rest_api_start
  (event loop created buried inside rest_api_start)

## Fix
Move esp_event_loop_create_default() to main.c, before
device_config_init(), matching the plan. Remove it from
rest_api_start(). This ensures the event loop exists for any
component that needs it.

## Impact
Medium — will cause a bug when network_init is implemented. The
network component will either fail to register event handlers or
will have to create its own event loop instance, breaking the
single-loop design.
close_reason: Fixed — main.c now creates default event loop at line 53, before any component init

title: cli: DeviceContext JSON tag fw_version mismatches plan's firmware_version
description:
## What is wrong
The CLI's DeviceContext struct in client/client.go:40 uses:
  FirmwareVersion string `json:"fw_version,omitempty"`

But the plan's robot envelope (Step 12c) specifies:
  "device_context": { "firmware_version": "0.3.1" }

And the firmware's own status endpoint in rest_api.c:151 uses:
  cJSON_AddStringToObject(root, "firmware_version", ...)

So three representations exist:
- CLI DeviceContext JSON:   fw_version      (extracted from headers)
- Plan robot envelope:      firmware_version (specified contract)
- Firmware status JSON:     firmware_version (REST response body)

The CLI JSON tag must be "firmware_version" to match the plan's robot
envelope contract. Agents parsing the robot envelope will look for
"firmware_version" and find nothing.

## Fix
Change the JSON tag in client/client.go:40 from
  `json:"fw_version,omitempty"`
to
  `json:"firmware_version,omitempty"`

## Impact
High — this is an API contract mismatch that will break agent parsing
of the robot envelope once both sides ship.
close_reason: Changed DeviceContext JSON output to firmware_version and added a client-package regression test so the robot envelope matches the documented firmware_version contract.

title: cli: timeout default 10s hardcoded in both config.DefaultTimeout and client.New fallback
description:
## What is wrong
The 10-second timeout default is defined in two places:

1. cli/internal/config/config.go:27
   var DefaultTimeout = 10 * time.Second

2. cli/client/client.go:53
   case timeout == 0:
       timeout = 10 * time.Second

config.Resolve() ensures timeout > 0 before returning, so client.New()
should never see timeout == 0 through the normal config pipeline. But
client.New() has its own independent 10s fallback for the zero case.

If someone changes DefaultTimeout in config.go (e.g., to 30s), the
client's hardcoded 10s literal won't match. Code that bypasses config
resolution (tests, future direct client usage) gets a different default.

## Fix
Replace the literal in client.New() with a reference to a shared
constant, or remove the client-side fallback entirely (since config
resolution guarantees timeout > 0) and instead validate that timeout
is non-zero in client.New() without defaulting.
close_reason: client.New now requires a positive timeout so config resolution remains the single source of truth for defaults

title: CI/CD & Release Pipeline (Phase 2b)
description: Unified CI/CD pipeline: conventional commits, path-filtered GitHub Actions CI (firmware build via esp-idf-ci-action, Go lint+test+build), tag-driven release workflow (GoReleaser for 6-platform CLI binaries, esp-idf for versioned firmware, git-cliff for changelog), and single-tag version management (vX.Y.Z drives everything).

title: Conventional commits convention and documentation
description:
Establish and document the conventional commits format used by git-cliff and the team.

## What
- Document commit message format: <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>
- Scopes: firmware, cli, or omit for cross-cutting
- Types: feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, ci, test, build (included in changelog), chore (filtered out)
- BREAKING CHANGE: via ! suffix or footer
- This is a convention/process task — no code to write

## Why
git-cliff parses these commit messages to auto-generate changelogs. Without a consistent format, the changelog is garbage. Conventional commits also make git log more scannable.

## Considerations
- This convention must be adopted BEFORE the first release tag — retroactively reformatting git history is painful
- The type-to-changelog group mapping must match the git-cliff configuration exactly
close_reason: Documented conventional commits and changelog type mapping in AGENTS.md

title: CI workflow — GitHub Actions with path filtering
description:
Continuous integration pipeline that builds and tests on every push/PR.

## What
- .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Triggers: push to main, PRs targeting main
- Permissions: contents:read, pull-requests:read
- Path filtering via dorny/paths-filter@v3 (firmware changes skip Go jobs, vice versa)
- Jobs:
  1. changes: detect which paths changed (outputs firmware/cli/shared booleans)
  2. firmware-build: espressif/esp-idf-ci-action@v1 (v5.4), set-target esp32, build, size report, upload artifact
  3. cli-lint: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9
  4. cli-test: go test -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
  5. cli-build: go build -o /dev/null .
- Go jobs use actions/setup-go@v6 with go-version-file: cli/go.mod
- All jobs start with actions/checkout@v6

## Why
CI catches build failures and regressions before they hit main. Path filtering avoids wasting CI minutes — firmware-only PRs don't need to lint Go code.

## Considerations
- The changes job uses dorny/paths-filter which needs a checkout for push-based detection
- shared paths (.github/workflows/**, cli/.goreleaser.yaml, cliff.toml) trigger both stacks
- firmware-build logs partition and binary sizes while .elf/.map are still present — important for OTA slot sizing validation

Verification: python3 YAML parse, actionlint via go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@latest .github/workflows/ci.yml, and . "/home/ubuntu/esp/esp-idf/export.sh" >/dev/null && just ci all passed.

title: GoReleaser v2 configuration for CLI releases
description:
GoReleaser configuration for building 6-platform CLI binaries.

## What
- cli/.goreleaser.yaml (GoReleaser v2 format)
- project_name: evb-relay (keeps archive names aligned with docs)
- binary: evb-relay (matches CLI command name)
- 6 targets: linux/darwin/windows x amd64/arm64
- CGO_ENABLED=0 for static binaries
- -trimpath + commit-derived timestamps for near-reproducible builds
- ldflags: inject Version, Commit, Date into cmd package
- Archives: .tar.gz (Unix), .zip (Windows)
- checksum.name_template: checksums.txt
- release.draft: true (release workflow marks as non-draft later)
- prerelease: auto (tags with -rc/-beta get pre-release flag)
- changelog: disabled (git-cliff handles it)

## Why
GoReleaser automates the tedious cross-compilation and artifact packaging. The release workflow delegates CLI binary production entirely to GoReleaser.

## Considerations
- The release workflow runs GoReleaser from cli/, so main: . resolves correctly
- draft: true is critical — the release workflow's final job marks the release as non-draft after adding firmware artifacts and changelog
- Version injection via ldflags must match the cmd package's var names exactly

title: git-cliff configuration for changelog generation
description:
Automated changelog generation from conventional commits.

## What
- cliff.toml at project root
- Conventional commit parser with type-to-group mapping
- Groups: Features (feat), Bug Fixes (fix), Refactoring (refactor), Performance (perf), Documentation (docs), CI/CD (ci), Testing (test), Build System (build)
- chore commits filtered out (skip: true)
- Scope renders inline: **firmware**: Add SSE heartbeat
- filter_unconventional = true (non-conventional commits excluded)
- Template uses Tera (Jinja2-like) for rendering

## Why
Hand-written changelogs are tedious and inconsistent. git-cliff generates them from commit messages, which we already structure via conventional commits.

## Considerations
- The group mapping must exactly match the conventional commits convention defined in the team docs
- Scopes (firmware, cli) render inline so firmware-only and CLI-only changes are visually distinct
- filter_unconventional=true means sloppy commit messages are silently dropped from the changelog — this is intentional
notes: 2026-03-18: adding cliff.toml with git-cliff's conventional commit parsing, the documented type-to-group mapping, chore filtering, and a template that renders scopes inline so firmware-only and CLI-only changes stay visually distinct in generated release notes.
close_reason: Added a root cliff.toml that maps the documented conventional commit types into release-note groups, skips chore commits, filters unconventional history, and renders scopes inline in generated changelog entries; validated the config structure with python3 TOML parsing.

title: Version management — single tag drives everything
description:
Unified version management where one git tag vX.Y.Z drives firmware and CLI versions.

## What
- Single source of truth: the git tag vX.Y.Z
- Firmware: release workflow passes -DPROJECT_VER=X.Y.Z to idf.py build, fills esp_app_desc_t.version
- firmware/version.txt: contains 0.0.0-dev as local dev fallback when PROJECT_VER is not injected
- CLI: GoReleaser injects version via ldflags into cmd.Version, cmd.Commit, cmd.Date
- Semver policy:
  - Major: breaking REST API changes, breaking CLI interface changes
  - Minor: new endpoints, new commands, new features
  - Patch: bug fixes, docs, internal refactors

## Why
One version number for both firmware and CLI simplifies compatibility tracking. Users can match CLI version to firmware version without a separate compatibility matrix.

## Considerations
- firmware/version.txt is ONLY for local dev builds — release builds always get the version from the tag
- The CLI's --version and --robot-capabilities both read from the same cmd package metadata
- Semver policy must be documented and followed — REST API changes are the most sensitive (agents depend on stable error codes and response schemas)
notes: 2026-03-18: adding the firmware version.txt dev fallback, documenting the single-tag version and semver policy in AGENTS.md, and aligning the CLI's default version string with the same 0.0.0-dev local-build convention used by firmware when release injection is absent.
close_reason: Added firmware/version.txt as the local PROJECT_VER fallback, aligned the CLI's default Version string with the same 0.0.0-dev convention, documented the single-tag version and semver policy in AGENTS.md, and verified with just ci.

title: Release workflow — tag-driven multi-artifact GitHub Release
description:
Tag-push-triggered workflow that builds versioned firmware, CLI binaries, and changelog into a GitHub Release.

## What
- .github/workflows/release.yml
- Trigger: tag push matching v*
- Permissions: contents:write
- Extracts version from tag (GITHUB_REF_NAME stripped of v prefix)
- All jobs use actions/checkout@v6 with fetch-depth: 0 (full tag history for GoReleaser + git-cliff)
- Jobs:
  1. firmware: esp-idf-ci-action with -DPROJECT_VER, rename to esp32-evb-relay-vX.Y.Z.bin, generate .sha256, upload artifacts
  2. cli: GoReleaser creates draft GitHub Release with 6 CLI archives + checksums.txt
  3. changelog: git-cliff --latest --strip header
  4. release (depends on 1-3): download firmware + changelog artifacts, upload firmware to the release, set body from changelog, mark release as non-draft

## Why
One git tag push produces a complete release: firmware binary, CLI binaries for 6 platforms, checksums, and auto-generated changelog. No manual steps after tagging.

## Considerations
- The firmware binary is app-only (suitable for OTA updates on already-provisioned devices) — first-time blank-device flashing uses local idf.py build outputs
- fetch-depth: 0 is required for GoReleaser (needs tags) and git-cliff (needs commit history)
- GoReleaser creates the release as draft; the final release job adds firmware, sets changelog, and marks non-draft
- Pre-release tags (v0.2.0-rc.1) get the pre-release flag via GoReleaser's prerelease: auto

## Release assets
- esp32-evb-relay-vX.Y.Z.bin + .sha256 (firmware)
- evb-relay_X.Y.Z_{os}_{arch}.tar.gz/.zip (6 CLI archives)
- checksums.txt (CLI archive checksums)

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
RELEASE PIPELINE — End-to-End Flow:

The release is triggered by pushing a tag: git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0

1. firmware job: builds with -DPROJECT_VER=0.1.0, produces esp32-evb-relay-v0.1.0.bin + .sha256
2. cli job: GoReleaser builds 6 platform binaries, creates a DRAFT GitHub Release
3. changelog job: git-cliff --latest generates release notes from conventional commits since the previous tag
4. release job (depends on 1-3): downloads firmware artifact + changelog, uploads firmware binary + checksum to the draft release, sets the release body from git-cliff output, marks release as non-draft

KEY INVARIANT: GoReleaser creates the release as a draft. The final release job adds firmware artifacts and changelog, then publishes. If the firmware build fails, the release stays as a draft and is not published with only CLI artifacts.

EDGE CASES:
- Pre-release tags (v0.2.0-rc.1): GoReleaser auto-marks as pre-release
- First-time flash: the released .bin is app-only (for OTA on provisioned devices). First-time blank-device flashing needs local idf.py outputs or a future factory-flash bundle.

title: firmware: auth_generate_token ignores buffer_size parameter — misleading API
description:
## What is wrong
auth.c:18-30 — auth_generate_token accepts a buffer_size parameter
but never uses it. The function writes exactly 33 bytes (32 hex chars
+ null terminator) unconditionally:

  static void auth_generate_token(char *buffer, size_t buffer_size)
  {
      ...
      buffer[sizeof(random_bytes) * 2U] = '\\0';
      (void)buffer_size;  // explicitly suppressed
  }

The single call site (line 76) passes a 256-byte buffer, so no
overflow occurs. But the API promises a safety check that does not
exist. A future caller with a smaller buffer (e.g., char buf[16])
would silently overflow.

## Fix options
a) Add a guard: if (buffer_size < AUTH_FIRST_BOOT_TOKEN_LEN + 1U)
   return; (and change return type to esp_err_t)
b) Remove the buffer_size parameter since output size is constant
   and the function is static (file-scoped)

Suggested: (b) — simplest, since the function is static and
the output size (AUTH_FIRST_BOOT_TOKEN_LEN + 1) is a compile-time
constant.

title: Scaffold ESP-IDF project
description:
Create the ESP-IDF v5.x project skeleton that everything else builds on.

## What
- firmware/CMakeLists.txt (top-level) + firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt
- sdkconfig.defaults: 4MB flash, custom partition table, Ethernet EMAC enabled, task watchdog, OTA rollback support (CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE)

Every firmware component depends on this scaffold. It sets the memory layout (partition table), the build system, and the baseline SDK configuration. Getting partitions right now avoids painful OTA size issues later.

title: REST API — onboard relay endpoints
description:
REST endpoints for the 2 onboard relays (GPIO32, GPIO33).

## What
- GET /api/v1/relays/onboard: list both onboard relay states
- PUT /api/v1/relays/onboard/{id}: set relay state {"state": true/false}
- POST /api/v1/relays/onboard/{id}/toggle: toggle relay
- Relay state changes publish relay_changed events to the internal event queue
- Part of the combined GET /api/v1/relays response (onboard + MOD-IO)
- 404 RELAY_NOT_FOUND for invalid IDs

## Why
Onboard relays are the simplest, always-available actuators. They serve as the basic validation that the full REST stack works end-to-end.

## Considerations
- IDs are 1-based at the API (onboard:1=GPIO32, onboard:2=GPIO33)
- Onboard relays have no 'unknown' state — they're GPIO-driven and we set them at boot
- Each relay change must publish an event so SSE clients see it in real-time

title: REST API — MOD-IO relay endpoints with authoritative readback model
description:
REST endpoints for the 4 MOD-IO relays using the board's authoritative relay-state readback.

## What
- GET /api/v1/relays/modio: current relay states when MOD-IO is present
- PUT /api/v1/relays/modio/{id}: set one MOD-IO relay via read-modify-write against the authoritative bitmap from command `0x40`
- PUT /api/v1/relays/modio: bulk set all 4 relays `{"states": [true,false,true,false]}` for efficient batched updates
- `503 MODIO_NOT_PRESENT`: when the daughterboard is physically absent
- Part of the combined GET /api/v1/relays response
- Relay changes publish `relay_changed` events to the event queue

## Why
Hardware command `0x40` provides the current 4-bit relay bitmap. The API should use that authoritative state instead of forcing clients through a synthetic unknown/synchronized recovery flow after reboot or reattach.

## Considerations
- Single-relay PUT must read the current bitmap, modify one bit, and write the full bitmap because the I2C protocol still only accepts full-mask writes
- Bulk PUT remains useful for batching and avoiding transient intermediate states, but it is no longer a recovery prerequisite
- On boot or hot reattach, the firmware should refresh relay state from readback rather than returning `409` or null placeholders
- Do NOT fabricate zeroed relay states when MOD-IO is absent

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
DESIGN RATIONALE — MOD-IO Sync State Model:

The three states (unknown, synchronized, absent) exist because of a hardware limitation: MOD-IO provides no relay-state readback command. The host writes a full 4-bit bitmap but cannot verify what the relays are actually doing.

State transitions:
- BOOT/REATTACH → unknown: After ESP32 reboot or MOD-IO hot-reattach, the host's RAM bitmap is stale. The actual hardware state is unknowable.
- BULK PUT → synchronized: When a client sends all 4 relay states in one PUT /api/v1/relays/modio, the firmware writes the bitmap and trusts it as authoritative.
- DISCONNECT → absent: MOD-IO is physically removed or I2C probe fails.

Why 409 on single-relay operations when unknown: If the host last knew [on,off,on,off] but the MOD-IO was power-cycled, the actual state might be [off,off,off,off]. If a client says 'set relay 1 to on', the firmware would read its stale RAM bitmap [on,off,on,off], set bit 0 to on (no change), and write [on,off,on,off] — potentially energizing relays 2 and 3 that the user didn't intend. Requiring the full bitmap forces the client to be explicit about ALL relay states.

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text: Design correction: command 0x40 provides authoritative relay state. The older sync-state rationale in this thread is superseded; this API should refresh from hardware readback instead of requiring a synthetic bulk-resync step. Follow-up firmware bug: evb-1gp.23.

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text: Correction: evb-1gp.22 is the canonical firmware follow-up for authoritative 0x40 relay readback. evb-1gp.23 was a duplicate and is closed.

title: REST API — input endpoints (digital + analog)
description:
REST endpoints serving MOD-IO digital and analog input snapshots.

## What
- GET /api/v1/inputs/digital: all 4 digital inputs from latest sampled snapshot + sample_ts_ms + staleness metadata
- GET /api/v1/inputs/digital/{id}: single digital input from snapshot
- GET /api/v1/inputs/analog: all 4 analog inputs (10-bit values) from latest snapshot + sample_ts_ms + staleness
- GET /api/v1/inputs/analog/{id}: single analog input from snapshot
- Serve from input_monitor's shared snapshot (do NOT trigger separate I2C reads per request)
- 503 MODIO_SAMPLE_UNAVAILABLE if no valid sample exists yet (retryable: true)
- 503 MODIO_NOT_PRESENT if daughterboard is absent

## Why
Input monitoring is the read-side complement to relay control. The snapshot-based approach avoids hammering the I2C bus — input_monitor polls at the configured interval and these endpoints just read the latest cached data.

## Considerations
- Sample staleness metadata helps clients assess data freshness — if poll_interval_ms is 100ms and the sample is 5000ms old, something is wrong
- 1-based IDs at the API, mapped to MOD-IO channels 0-3 internally
- Do NOT pretend an old or nonexistent snapshot is current — return 503 MODIO_SAMPLE_UNAVAILABLE instead

title: REST API — SSE event stream with fan-out and backpressure
description:
Server-Sent Events endpoint for real-time push notifications.

## What
- GET /api/v1/events (Accept: text/event-stream)
- Long-lived HTTP connection, server pushes SSE-framed JSON payloads
- Dedicated event-dispatch path inside rest_api drains the internal event queue and fans out copies to connected SSE clients
- Individual HTTP handlers must NOT consume the producer queue directly
- Event types: digital_input, analog_input, relay_changed, button
- Format: event: digital_input\ndata: {"id":2,"state":true,"ts_ms":12345}\n\n
- Cap SSE fan-out to a small fixed number of clients (MCU resource constraint)
- Drop stale subscribers on backpressure instead of letting one slow client exhaust resources
- 30s heartbeat to detect stale connections

## Why
Firmware polls MOD-IO over I2C (no interrupt line), but SSE makes the CLIENT event-driven. This is the key architectural inversion: clients don't need to poll the REST API — they subscribe once and get real-time push notifications.

## Considerations
- The ESP32 has limited RAM — cap concurrent SSE clients (e.g., 4-8 max)
- The event queue is shared: input_monitor produces, relay setters produce, SSE dispatcher consumes and fans out
- Backpressure handling is critical: one slow WiFi client must not block events for all other clients
- Heartbeat (comment line every 30s) detects dead TCP connections that the kernel hasn't noticed yet

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE — SSE Event Fan-Out:

The SSE system has three layers:

1. PRODUCERS (write to shared event queue):
   - input_monitor: digital_input, analog_input, button events
   - relay setters (relay.c, mod_io.c): relay_changed events
   
2. DISPATCHER (single consumer of the queue):
   - A dedicated task inside rest_api drains the event queue
   - Copies each event to all connected SSE client buffers
   - Individual HTTP handlers must NEVER consume from the queue directly
   
3. SSE CLIENTS (fan-out targets):
   - Each GET /api/v1/events connection gets its own small ring buffer
   - The dispatcher writes to each client buffer
   - Each client's HTTP send loop reads from its own buffer

BACKPRESSURE: If a client's buffer fills up (slow reader), that client is dropped rather than blocking the dispatcher. This prevents one slow client from starving all others.

CLIENT CAP: Hard limit on concurrent SSE connections (4-8) because each consumes a persistent HTTP connection + buffer + task stack on the ESP32's limited RAM.

HEARTBEAT: Every 30s, the dispatcher sends an SSE comment line (:heartbeat\n\n) to all clients. If the TCP write fails, the client is considered dead and cleaned up.

title: REST API — config endpoints (read/write with live-apply metadata)
description:
REST endpoints for reading and writing device configuration.

## What
- GET /api/v1/config: validated, redacted config — poll_interval_ms, hostname, modio_boot_policy, api_token_set (boolean, never the actual token)
- PUT /api/v1/config: update config {"poll_interval_ms": 200} — returns which changes applied live vs require restart
- Reads from and writes to device_config component
- Validates input before persisting

## Why
Runtime configurability without reflashing. The live-vs-restart metadata is critical for UX — changing poll_interval_ms can take effect immediately, but changing hostname requires mDNS re-registration.

## Considerations
- NEVER echo api_token back — expose only api_token_set: true/false
- The response must clearly indicate {"live": true/false} per changed key
- Validation happens in device_config, not in the HTTP handler — keep the handler thin

title: OTA component — firmware update with rollback protection
description:
Over-the-air firmware update via HTTP upload with automatic rollback.

## What
- POST /api/v1/ota: streams binary via esp_ota_begin/write/end
- Sets boot partition to the newly written OTA slot, reboots after 2s delay
- On next boot: call esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback() ONLY after bounded local startup health checks pass:
  - Config loaded
  - Board/peripheral init succeeded
  - Background tasks started
  - Ethernet driver initialized
- Do NOT make rollback confirmation depend on external conditions (DHCP, mDNS) — those can fail transiently without indicating a bad firmware image
- Rollback enabled via CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE in sdkconfig.defaults
- Lives in firmware/components/ota/

## Why
OTA is the only way to update firmware without physical serial access. Rollback protection prevents a bad firmware update from bricking the device — if the new image can't initialize its core subsystems, the bootloader automatically reverts to the previous working image.

## Considerations
- The 2s reboot delay gives the HTTP response time to complete before the connection drops
- Health checks must be fast and bounded — don't wait for DHCP which could take 30+ seconds
- The OTA endpoint must validate the binary size against the partition table's OTA slot size before starting the write

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
OTA SAFETY — Rollback Confirmation Strategy:

The rollback mechanism is the device's self-healing capability against bad firmware updates. CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE makes the bootloader track whether the running image has been confirmed.

CONFIRMATION POINT: esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback() is called ONLY after:
1. NVS flash initialized successfully
2. device_config loaded
3. board_init completed (GPIOs, I2C bus)
4. relay_init completed
5. mod_io probed (can be absent — that's fine)
6. input_monitor task started
7. auth_init completed
8. Ethernet driver initialized

CRITICAL: Do NOT wait for DHCP, mDNS, or any external dependency. A legitimate firmware image can fail to get an IP temporarily (bad DHCP server, cable unplugged) but that doesn't mean it should be rolled back. Rollback should only trigger for genuinely broken firmware that can't even initialize its core subsystems.

If confirmation doesn't happen within the bootloader's timeout (default: one boot cycle), the bootloader automatically reverts to the previous OTA slot.

title: Boot sequence integration — main.c init orchestration
description:
The app_main() function that wires all firmware components together in the correct init order.

## What
- Init sequence: nvs_flash_init → event_loop_create → device_config_init → board_init → relay_init → mod_io_init → input_monitor_start → auth_init → network_init → ota_confirm_running_image_if_core_init_passed → wait_for_ip → mdns_register → rest_api_start
- Register long-running tasks (input_monitor, SSE dispatcher) with the task watchdog
- Handle init failures gracefully — if MOD-IO is absent, continue without it; if Ethernet fails, treat as startup failure

## Why
This is the integration point where all components come together. The init ORDER matters: device_config must load before anything reads config, board_init must run before relay/mod_io use GPIOs, network must be up before the REST API starts, and OTA rollback confirmation must happen after core init passes but before the device is considered operational.

## Considerations
- OTA rollback confirmation is specifically placed AFTER core init passes but BEFORE external dependencies (DHCP) are required — this prevents a transient network issue from triggering an unnecessary rollback
- MOD-IO absence is graceful (the device still works with just onboard relays)
- Ethernet failure is fatal in Phase 1 (no WiFi fallback)

title: Provisioning and flash scripts
description:
Shell scripts for initial device setup and credential management.

## What
- scripts/flash.sh: wrapper around idf.py flash for convenient first-time flashing
- scripts/provision.sh: set or rotate API token over serial connection for provisioning/service
  - Can be used when the first-boot token was missed
  - Can rotate tokens without reflashing
  - Uses serial console to communicate with the running firmware

## Why
The device needs a physical provisioning path for first-boot setup and token recovery. Without provision.sh, a lost API token means reflashing the entire firmware (or wiping NVS manually).

## Considerations
- provision.sh must work with the device's serial console — it writes commands that the firmware's serial handler processes
- The firmware side needs a corresponding serial command handler (or NVS partition write utility)
- These scripts are host-platform-dependent (serial device paths vary: /dev/tty.usbserial-* on macOS, /dev/ttyUSB* on Linux)

title: REST API should fail closed when no auth handler is configured
description:
Current firmware boots the HTTP server with no auth callback configured, and `rest_api_authorize_request()` treats a missing handler as allow.

Code references:
- firmware/main/main.c:11-13,28
- firmware/components/rest_api/rest_api.c:107-113

Why this is a problem:
- A freshly flashed device exposes `/api/v1/status` publicly until the auth component is wired in.
- This is a fail-open default in the control plane, which is the wrong safety posture for a device intended to use bearer auth.

Expected direction:
- Default to deny or refuse to start the API server unless an explicit auth strategy is installed.

title: Status endpoint should not fabricate network and MOD-IO state
description:
The status endpoint currently synthesizes `network.connected=false`, empty IP fields, `modio.present=false`, and `modio.sync=absent` whenever no status provider is registered.

Code references:
- firmware/main/main.c:11-13
- firmware/components/rest_api/rest_api.c:69-83,154-163

Why this is a problem:
- Clients receive authoritative-looking false negatives instead of a clear "unavailable/unwired" signal.
- Once flashed, the current binary can report that Ethernet is down and MOD-IO is absent even when later components are actually working but have not been wired into `rest_api_config_t`.

Expected direction:
- Do not fabricate device state from zeroed defaults.
- Require a status provider, or represent unavailable state explicitly in the payload.

title: Board component — pin definitions and I2C bus init
description:
Hardware abstraction layer defining ESP32-EVB pin assignments and initializing shared peripherals.

## What
- Pin constants: BOARD_RELAY1_GPIO=32, BOARD_RELAY2_GPIO=33, BOARD_I2C_SDA=13, BOARD_I2C_SCL=16, BOARD_ETH_MDC=23, BOARD_ETH_MDIO=18, BOARD_BUTTON=34
- board_init(): configure I2C master bus at 100kHz, configure button GPIO input
- Lives in firmware/components/board/

## Why
Centralizes hardware-specific constants so no other component hard-codes pin numbers. The I2C bus handle created here is shared by mod_io and potentially future UEXT peripherals.

## Considerations
- ESP32-EVB uses UEXT connector for I2C (SDA=GPIO13, SCL=GPIO16) — these are fixed by the board layout, not configurable
- Button is on GPIO34 (input-only GPIO on ESP32, no internal pull-up available on 34-39)
- Use ESP-IDF v5.x i2c_master API, not the deprecated i2c_cmd_link driver

title: Board layer should centralize the canonical 100 kHz I2C device speed
description:
The board component declares `BOARD_I2C_SCL_SPEED_HZ` as the canonical 100 kHz bus speed, but `board_init()` does not enforce or propagate that invariant to downstream devices.

Code references:
- firmware/components/board/include/board.h:19-20
- firmware/components/board/board.c:24-31

Why this is a problem:
- In ESP-IDF v5.x, I2C speed is configured per device, not on the bus object.
- Future consumers can silently add devices at a different speed while the board layer still logs/advertises 100 kHz, which defeats the point of centralizing hardware defaults.

Expected direction:
- Expose a board-level helper/config for creating I2C devices with the canonical speed, or remove the misleading invariant from the board API.
notes: 2026-03-18: implementing a board-owned I2C device config helper so downstream devices inherit BOARD_I2C_SCL_SPEED_HZ instead of hardcoding 100000U locally. Plan includes a narrow board device regression test for the new public API.

title: Device config apply metadata cannot represent deferred-on-next-boot changes
description:
`device_config_apply_result_t` only models `{live, restart_required}`. That cannot express settings that are neither live-applied nor restart-required, but instead only affect future boot behavior.

Code references:
- firmware/components/device_config/include/device_config.h:33-36
- firmware/components/device_config/device_config.c:63-72,167-175

Why this is a problem:
- `modio_boot_policy` currently reports `live=false` and `restart_required=false`, which is ambiguous for API/CLI users.
- The current shape cannot clearly distinguish "already applied", "requires immediate restart", and "takes effect on next relevant boot/event".

Expected direction:
- Replace the boolean pair with a clearer apply-mode enum or richer result schema before REST/CLI config endpoints depend on it.
notes: 2026-03-18: replacing the ambiguous live/restart_required boolean pair with an explicit apply-mode enum so config consumers can distinguish immediate, restart-gated, and deferred-on-next-boot behavior before REST/CLI config endpoints depend on the old shape.
close_reason: Replaced the ambiguous live/restart_required boolean pair with an explicit apply-mode enum, marked modio_boot_policy as next_boot, and added host regression coverage for the new metadata contract.

title: firmware: mod_io should use authoritative 0x40 relay readback
description:
## What is wrong

The project has now reconciled the MOD-IO protocol docs around command `0x40`
relay-state readback, but the production `mod_io` component still models the
board as if relay state were unknowable after boot or hot reattach.

Current code keeps an `unknown/synchronized/absent` state machine and forces
single-relay operations to depend on cached RAM state instead of reloading the
authoritative hardware bitmap.

## Where

- firmware/components/mod_io/mod_io.c
- firmware/components/mod_io/include/mod_io.h
- firmware/main/main.c
- Any API surface that still treats `unknown` as a required recovery state

## Fix

- Add a public/internal path to read the authoritative relay bitmap via
  command `0x40`
- Refresh the cached relay bitmap after init and after MOD-IO reattach
- Use read-modify-write for single-relay updates against authoritative state
- Collapse or narrow the synthetic `unknown` state so product behavior matches
  the confirmed hardware protocol

## Why

Leaving the old model in code would bake avoidable tech debt into the driver,
REST API, CLI, and tests. The firmware should use the hardware capability that
actually exists.

## Impact

This blocks the final shape of:
- evb-1gp.11 (REST API MOD-IO relay endpoints)
- evb-2ee.6 (host MOD-IO tests)
- evb-2ee.11 (device MOD-IO tests)
close_reason: Implemented authoritative 0x40 relay readback in mod_io, removed the deprecated unknown sync state from firmware/REST surfaces, and refreshed status requests through mod_io_probe() so cached presence and relay state stay aligned with hardware.

title: firmware: replace MOD-IO unknown-state cache with authoritative 0x40 readback
description:
## What is wrong

The project docs now treat MOD-IO command `0x40` relay-state readback as
authoritative, but the current `mod_io` component still implements the older
unknown/synchronized/absent cache model.

Current code paths still assume readback does not exist:
- `firmware/components/mod_io/include/mod_io.h`
- `firmware/components/mod_io/mod_io.c`
- `firmware/main/main.c`

This means the firmware can still expose stale or null relay-state semantics
after boot or reconnect even though the hardware can report the real bitmap.

## Fix

- Add authoritative relay-state refresh based on command `0x40`
- Seed cached relay state from hardware readback during init and after a
  successful reprobe/reconnect
- Make single-relay operations perform read-modify-write against fresh
  readback state
- Remove the synthetic unknown-state recovery path from the component's
  public behavior and any dependent firmware surfaces

## Why

Leaving the old state model in place would preserve avoidable tech debt in the
core MOD-IO driver, keep QA assertions ambiguous, and push the wrong recovery
contract into the REST API and CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mod_io` exposes authoritative relay state after init when the board is present
- Reconnect/reprobe path refreshes relay state from readback instead of null/unknown placeholders
- Single-relay operations no longer depend on a stale cached bitmap
- Firmware surfaces depending on `mod_io` can stop modeling a synthetic unknown state
close_reason: Duplicate of evb-1gp.22

title: Onboard relay GPIO driver
description:
Driver for the 2 onboard relays on GPIO32 and GPIO33.

## What
- relay_init(): configure GPIOs as output, drive both to OFF at boot
- relay_set(id, state): set relay on/off
- relay_get(id): read current state from in-memory tracking
- relay_toggle(id): flip current state
- Mutex for thread safety (REST handlers + SSE + boot code all access relays)
- Lives in firmware/components/relay/

## Why
Onboard relays are the simplest actuators and the first thing users will test. Boot-default OFF is critical safety behavior — an ESP32 reboot must not accidentally energize loads.

## Considerations
- State is tracked in RAM after init (GPIOs are output, we set them, so we know the state)
- relay_set publishes relay_changed events into the shared internal event queue (used by SSE)
- IDs are 1-based at the API layer (onboard:1, onboard:2), mapped to GPIO32/GPIO33 internally
- Do NOT store relay state in NVS — unnecessary flash wear for volatile runtime state
close_reason: Completed

title: MOD-IO I2C protocol driver
description:
I2C driver for Olimex MOD-IO expansion board (I2C slave address 0x58).

## What
- Uses ESP-IDF v5.x i2c_master API (NOT deprecated i2c_cmd_link)
- I2C protocol commands:
  - 0x10 + bitmask: set relay outputs (bits 0-3, full 4-bit bitmap each write)
  - 0x40: read the current relay-state bitmask from hardware
  - 0x20: read digital inputs (1 byte, 4 inputs)
  - 0x30-0x33: select analog input 1-4, then read two bytes — decode the 10-bit sample from MOD-IO's LSB:MSB bit-packed format explicitly, do NOT treat as plain host-endian uint16
- mod_io_init(bus_handle): takes I2C bus handle from board component
- mod_io_is_present(): probe for device on bus
- Graceful degradation when MOD-IO is physically absent
- Cache relay bitmap in RAM, but treat hardware readback as authoritative after init, probe, and reconnect
- Serialize ALL I2C transactions inside the component (mutex) so polling and request handlers never race on the shared bus
- Lives in firmware/components/mod_io/

## Why
MOD-IO provides 4 additional relays + 4 digital inputs + 4 analog inputs over I2C. The deployed board supports authoritative relay-state readback, so new work should use that capability instead of preserving a synthetic unknown-state recovery model.

## Considerations
- The write command ALWAYS sends the full 4-bit relay bitmap — there is no single-relay write
- Do NOT write every relay toggle to NVS to simulate readback — that creates flash wear without making the state authoritative
- After hot reattach, refresh from readback and do NOT replay modio_boot_policy against a newly reappearing board
- The analog input decoding is a specific gotcha: MOD-IO manual documents a particular bit-packed LSB:MSB format for the 10-bit ADC samples

## Historical note
The first implementation of this bead landed before the readback reconciliation. Follow-up bug evb-1gp.22 tracks bringing the production component fully in line with the confirmed protocol.
close_reason: Implemented firmware/components/mod_io with ESP-IDF v5 I2C transactions, cached presence/sync state, serialized relay/input access, and boot/status integration; verified with firmware build

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES — MOD-IO I2C Protocol:

The MOD-IO uses Olimex's custom I2C protocol at slave address 0x58. Key operations:

RELAY WRITE (0x10): Send [0x10, bitmask]. Bitmask bits 0-3 map to relays 1-4. The protocol ALWAYS sends the full 4-bit bitmap — there is no single-relay write command. This is why the firmware keeps a RAM copy of the bitmap and modifies individual bits before sending the full byte.

DIGITAL INPUT READ (0x20): Send [0x20], read 1 byte. Bits 0-3 represent inputs 1-4.

ANALOG INPUT READ (0x30-0x33): Send [0x30+channel], then read 2 bytes. The 10-bit ADC sample is bit-packed in the MOD-IO manual's LSB:MSB format. This is NOT a standard little-endian uint16 — the bits must be unpacked according to the manual's specific layout. Get this wrong and analog readings will be garbage.

STATE MODEL: There is no readback command for relay state. After power loss or bus reset, the MOD-IO relays may be in any state, but the host has no way to query what state they're in. This is the fundamental reason for the 'unknown' state model — it's not a software choice, it's a hardware constraint.

I2C SERIALIZATION: All transactions must be serialized with a mutex because the input_monitor task polls inputs on a timer while REST handlers may write relays at any time. Two concurrent I2C transactions on the same bus will corrupt each other.

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text: Design correction: MOD-IO command 0x40 relay-state readback is authoritative. This bead landed under the earlier write-only assumption; follow-up bug evb-1gp.23 tracks aligning the component implementation with the corrected hardware model.

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text: Correction: evb-1gp.22 is the canonical follow-up bead for aligning the production MOD-IO component with authoritative 0x40 readback. evb-1gp.23 was a duplicate and is closed.

title: Device config component — NVS-backed runtime configuration
description:
Centralized, NVS-backed configuration store for all runtime settings.

## What
- NVS storage for: api_token, poll_interval_ms, hostname, modio_boot_policy, (future: WiFi credentials)
- Centralized validation, defaults, and persistence
- device_config_init(): load config from NVS, apply defaults for missing keys
- Getter/setter API for each config key with validation
- modio_boot_policy: enum {leave_unchanged, all_off} — defaults to leave_unchanged
- Secrets are write-only at the API layer: never echo api_token or raw WiFi credentials back
- Returns metadata about whether a config change is applied live or requires restart
- Lives in firmware/components/device_config/

## Why
Without centralization, auth, network, input_monitor, and rest_api would each manage their own ad hoc NVS keys — leading to inconsistent validation, scattered defaults, and no single place to understand the config schema.

## Considerations
- modio_boot_policy defaults to leave_unchanged so an ESP32 reboot does NOT silently toggle attached loads; all_off is an explicit opt-in for fail-safe-off behavior
- The 'applied live vs restart required' metadata is important for the REST API and CLI to communicate clearly to the user
- Future WiFi credentials will live here too — the component should be designed for extensibility
- Config keys should be documented in a central enum/struct, not scattered as string literals
close_reason: Completed

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
CONFIG DESIGN — modio_boot_policy Rationale:

The boot policy determines what happens to MOD-IO relays when the ESP32 reboots. Two options:

LEAVE_UNCHANGED (default): After reboot, MOD-IO relay state is marked 'unknown' and the firmware does NOT write any bitmap. The physical relays stay in whatever state they were in before the reboot. A client must explicitly send a bulk PUT to establish sync.

WHY THIS IS THE DEFAULT: Consider a MOD-IO controlling a heating element. If the ESP32 reboots (watchdog, OTA, power glitch), silently forcing all relays off could cause a temperature drop. Silently forcing them on could cause overheating. The safest option is to not touch them and require explicit human/agent intervention.

ALL_OFF: After reboot, immediately write [0,0,0,0] to MOD-IO relays and mark state as 'synchronized'. This is an explicit opt-in for fail-safe-off behavior — appropriate for loads where de-energized is always the safe state (e.g., test equipment, lighting).

IMPORTANT: After hot-reattach (MOD-IO was disconnected and reconnected while ESP32 was running), NEITHER policy is reapplied. The state goes to 'unknown' and requires explicit client action. This prevents the firmware from automatically energizing a freshly-connected board.

title: Input monitor component — polling, events, and button debounce
description:
FreeRTOS task that continuously polls MOD-IO inputs and publishes change events.

## What
- FreeRTOS task polling MOD-IO digital + analog inputs at configurable interval (default 100ms from device_config)
- Owns the latest sampled input snapshot and timestamps; REST endpoints serve this shared snapshot by default (no per-request I2C reads)
- Compares against previous state, publishes normalized events into a single internal event queue:
  - digital_input events (state change)
  - analog_input events (threshold-based change detection for 10-bit samples to avoid noise)
  - button events (GPIO34 interrupt + software debounce)
- Relay setters publish their own relay_changed events — input_monitor must NOT invent relay events
- If MOD-IO probing starts succeeding after absence/error: publish presence change, refresh the cached relay bitmap from command `0x40`, resume sampling WITHOUT reapplying modio_boot_policy
- Lives in firmware/components/input_monitor/

## Why
The internal event queue is the backbone of the SSE system. Clients see real-time state changes because input_monitor detects them and publishes events. The shared snapshot avoids hammering the I2C bus with redundant reads on every HTTP request.

## Considerations
- Analog threshold is configurable to avoid noise-triggered events (10-bit ADC on MOD-IO has inherent noise)
- Button debounce is critical — without it, one physical press fans out into multiple spurious events
- MOD-IO has no interrupt line, so polling is the only option for inputs
- The event queue is consumed by the SSE dispatcher in rest_api; input_monitor is the primary producer
- GPIO34 is input-only on ESP32 (no pull-up), so external pull-up or the board's pull-up circuit is relied upon

title: Network component — Ethernet init, IP wait, and mDNS
description:
Ethernet networking and service discovery for the ESP32-EVB.

## What
- Ethernet init: LAN8710A PHY at address 0, RMII clock input on GPIO0, MDC/MDIO on GPIO23/18
- PHY reset: reset_gpio_num = -1 (no dedicated ESP32-controlled reset GPIO on current ESP32-EVB revisions)
- Event-driven: register for IP_EVENT_ETH_GOT_IP
- network_wait_for_ip(timeout_ms): blocks app_main until connected or returns timeout/error
- In Ethernet-only phase, treat timeout as startup FAILURE — do not silently continue without a usable control plane
- mDNS: default hostname from device_config (default: esp32-evb-relay), register _http._tcp service with TXT records (fw_version, board type)
- Architecture allows later WiFi phase (separate init path, shared event handlers)
- Lives in firmware/components/network/

## Why
Ethernet is the control plane — without an IP, the REST API is unreachable and the device is inert. mDNS enables zero-configuration discovery by the CLI (evb-relay discover).

## Considerations
- The LAN8710A PHY configuration is specific to Olimex ESP32-EVB board layout — verify PHY address and clock mode against the schematic
- Do NOT silently continue if Ethernet fails to get an IP — the device has no WiFi fallback in Phase 1
- mDNS TXT records should include fw_version (from esp_app_desc_t) for the CLI discover command to display
close_reason: Implemented the production network component with Ethernet bring-up, IP wait, mDNS registration, and status wiring; firmware CI now passes with the new path in place.

title: Auth component — API token validation and first-boot provisioning
description:
Bearer token authentication for all REST API endpoints.

## What
- API token loaded from device_config at init
- auth_check(httpd_req_t*): validates Authorization: Bearer <token> header
- Protects all /api/v1/* endpoints
- Secure by default: on first boot, if no token exists, generate a random token, persist it to NVS, and print it ONCE on the serial console
- Constant-time comparison (timing-safe) to prevent timing attacks
- Define explicit recovery path for lost credentials: scripts/provision.sh sets/rotates token over serial
- Factory-reset path: clear token by wiping relevant NVS keys
- Lives in firmware/components/auth/

## Why
The device controls physical relays — unauthorized access could energize/de-energize loads with safety implications. Secure-by-default means the device is never exposed without auth, even on first boot.

## Considerations
- The first-boot token is printed to serial ONCE — if the user misses it, they need the provision.sh recovery path
- Constant-time comparison is critical even though this is a local network device — defense in depth
- auth_check must return 401/403 BEFORE any other processing; unauthenticated requests must not leak device metadata (no response headers on 401/403)
close_reason: Completed

title: REST API server core — HTTP server, error format, headers, status endpoint
description:
Foundation of the REST API: HTTP server setup, shared infrastructure, internal event system, and the status endpoint.

## What
- HTTP server init using ESP-IDF httpd
- GET /api/v1/status: uptime, FW version, network info, MOD-IO presence/sync state, free heap
- Response headers on all authenticated responses: X-FW-Version, X-ModIO-Present, X-ModIO-Sync (via post-handler hook)
  - Do NOT attach headers to pre-auth 401/403 responses
  - X-ModIO-Present and X-ModIO-Sync from mod_io component state
  - Under the confirmed readback model, X-ModIO-Sync is `synchronized` when MOD-IO is present/readable and `absent` otherwise
  - X-FW-Version from esp_app_desc_t.version
- Standardized error format: {"error": {"code": "RELAY_NOT_FOUND", "message": "...", "status": 404}}
- Internal event system: defines shared event types (digital_input, analog_input, relay_changed, button) and event struct in a public header; creates the default event loop (esp_event_loop_create_default) during init -- input_monitor and relay handlers produce events, the SSE dispatcher consumes and fans out
- URI parsing: httpd_uri_match_wildcard() + parse_id_from_uri() helper (ESP-IDF httpd lacks native path params)
- Public API uses 1-based IDs (onboard:1..2, modio:1..4, input 1..4); firmware maps internally to GPIO defs and MOD-IO protocol channels 0..3
- Lives in firmware/components/rest_api/ (shared core)

## Why
Every REST endpoint depends on this shared infrastructure: the HTTP server, auth middleware, error format, response headers, and event system. The status endpoint is the simplest read-only endpoint and validates the full stack (server + auth + headers).

## Considerations
- Response headers are essential for the CLI's robot mode: device_context is extracted from these headers, avoiding a sidecar /api/v1/status call
- The 1-based to 0-based ID mapping must be consistent across ALL endpoints
- Error codes must be stable strings (RELAY_NOT_FOUND, MODIO_NOT_PRESENT, etc.) because the CLI maps them to exit codes and remediation hints
- The event type header must be included by all producers (relay driver, input_monitor) and the SSE consumer -- define it in a shared include path within rest_api or a dedicated firmware/components/events/ component
close_reason: Completed

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
DESIGN NOTES — Response Headers:

X-FW-Version, X-ModIO-Present, X-ModIO-Sync are attached as HTTP response headers on all authenticated responses. This is the mechanism that enables the CLI's device_context in robot envelopes without making a separate GET /api/v1/status call.

Implementation: a post-handler hook or helper function that runs after the main handler. It checks if the response is authenticated (status is not 401/403) and if the handler succeeded or returned an application error (both get headers). Pre-auth 401/403 responses do NOT get headers because unauthenticated clients should not learn firmware/hardware metadata.

Header values:
- X-FW-Version: read from esp_app_desc_t.version (the running firmware's embedded version string)
- X-ModIO-Present: true/false from mod_io_is_present()
- X-ModIO-Sync: 'synchronized' | 'unknown' | 'absent' from the mod_io state machine

title: cli: go.mod needs go mod tidy — indirect markers wrong, unused hashicorp/mdns dep
description:
## What is wrong
All direct dependencies in cli/go.mod are marked `// indirect` even though cobra and toml are directly imported. Additionally, `hashicorp/mdns` and its 6 transitive dependencies (miekg/dns, x/mod, x/net, x/sync, x/sys, x/tools) are declared but no Go source file imports mdns — it was added prematurely for the future `discover` command.

## Why it matters
- Incorrect `// indirect` markers make it unclear which packages are actual direct deps vs transitive.
- The unused mdns tree inflates `go.sum` and pulls extra code during `go get`.
- Tools that parse go.mod (renovate, dependabot) treat indirect deps differently.

## Fix
Run `go mod tidy` in `cli/`. This:
1. Moves cobra and toml into a direct `require` block (no `// indirect`)
2. Removes hashicorp/mdns and its transitive deps entirely
3. Keeps mousetrap and pflag as proper indirect deps

Re-add mdns later when the `discover` command is implemented.

title: test: REST API device tests do not verify device context response headers
description:
## What is wrong
The plan (Step 7) says every authenticated REST API response must
include device context headers:
  X-FW-Version: <version>
  X-ModIO-Present: true|false
  X-ModIO-Sync: synchronized|unknown|absent

rest_api.c:88-105 (rest_api_try_attach_device_context_headers) sets
these headers on authenticated success responses and on post-auth
error responses. The CLI's DeviceContext extraction depends on them.

The REST API device test (test_rest_api_device.c) verifies:
- HTTP status (200, 401, 403)
- JSON body content (hostname, sync state)

But NO test checks whether the device context headers actually appear
in the response. A regression that breaks header injection (e.g.,
removing the rest_api_try_attach_device_context_headers call or
changing header names) would go undetected.

The perform_status_request() function already reads the complete
HTTP response (headers + body) into one buffer, so adding header
checks is straightforward.

## Fix
Add to the 200 OK test case:
  TEST_ASSERT_NOT_NULL(strstr(response, "X-FW-Version:"));
  TEST_ASSERT_NOT_NULL(strstr(response, "X-ModIO-Present: true"));
  TEST_ASSERT_NOT_NULL(strstr(response, "X-ModIO-Sync: synchronized"));

And verify they are ABSENT on 401/403 responses (the plan says
unauthenticated clients should not receive firmware/hardware
metadata).
close_reason: Added device tests for required context headers on authenticated responses and their absence on 401/403

title: cli: Cobra EnableTraverseRunHooks not set — subcommand PersistentPreRunE will skip config resolution
description:
## What is wrong
The root command defines PersistentPreRunE for config resolution. In
Cobra, if a subcommand defines its own PersistentPreRunE, it REPLACES
the parent's — the parent's hook is silently skipped.

This is a well-known Cobra footgun. Cobra v1.6.0+ (we use v1.10.2)
provides EnableTraverseRunHooks to opt in to parent hook chaining,
but the code does not set it.

When subcommands like 'relay' are added (which will have sub-sub-
commands and may need their own PersistentPreRunE for host validation),
config resolution will silently break unless:
a) EnableTraverseRunHooks is enabled, or
b) every subcommand carefully uses only PreRunE (not PersistentPreRunE)

## Where
cli/cmd/root.go — newRootCommand does not set
cobra.EnableTraverseRunHooks = true

## Fix
Add cobra.EnableTraverseRunHooks = true at the top of
newRootCommand (or in an init function). This is the modern Cobra
approach and ensures parent PersistentPreRunE always runs.

## Impact
Medium — not a bug today (no subcommands exist yet), but a trap that
will cause silent, hard-to-debug failures when subcommands are added.
Filing now to prevent it.
close_reason: newRootCommand now enables Cobra traverse run hooks

title: firmware: mod_io depends on board.h through fragile transitive REQUIRES chain
description:
## What is wrong
mod_io.c now includes board.h (added in commit ca2b0b0 to call
board_i2c_device_config) but mod_io's CMakeLists.txt does not list
board in REQUIRES:

  REQUIRES esp_driver_i2c esp_timer freertos rest_api

The include compiles because board is transitively reachable via:
  mod_io -> rest_api -> relay -> board

This is fragile. If rest_api ever removes relay from its REQUIRES
(e.g., relay endpoints move to a separate component), or if relay
removes board from its REQUIRES, mod_io fails to compile with a
missing header error. The three-hop chain is not documented and
not obvious.

## Fix
Add board to mod_io's REQUIRES:

  REQUIRES board esp_driver_i2c esp_timer freertos rest_api

This makes the dependency explicit and survives refactoring of
the rest_api or relay dependency chains.
notes: 2026-03-18: making the new mod_io -> board include dependency explicit in CMakeLists.txt so the component no longer relies on rest_api -> relay -> board transitively exposing board.h.
close_reason: Added board to mod_io's REQUIRES list so the component no longer depends on a fragile transitive include chain for board.h; verified with just ci.

title: build(cli): GoReleaser config missing dir field — build runs from wrong directory
description:
## What is wrong
cli/.goreleaser.yaml has:

  builds:
    - main: .
      binary: evb-relay

With no `dir` field, GoReleaser runs `go build .` from the project
root. But go.mod is in cli/, not the repo root:

  $ ls go.mod cli/go.mod
  go.mod: No such file
  cli/go.mod: exists

GoReleaser would fail with 'go.mod file not found in current directory'
because there is no Go module at the repository root.

## Fix
Add dir: cli to the build config:

  builds:
    - dir: cli
      main: .
      binary: evb-relay

This makes GoReleaser cd into cli/ before building, where go.mod
lives. All other fields (ldflags, env, etc.) are correct.
notes: 2026-03-18: root-level goreleaser build with --config cli/.goreleaser.yaml fails because the build runs outside the CLI module. Fixing by standardizing on repo-root invocation: add dir: cli in the GoReleaser build config and update the release-plan note that still says workdir: cli.
close_reason: Standardized the GoReleaser config on repo-root invocation by adding dir: cli, updated the release-plan note to match, and verified with goreleaser check plus a successful root-level goreleaser build --config cli/.goreleaser.yaml --snapshot --clean --single-target.

title: ci: astyle continuation indent mangles designated initializer in board.c button_config
description:
## What is wrong
board.c:17-23 — the button_config designated initializer has bizarre
deep indentation after the first field:

    const gpio_config_t button_config = {
        .pin_bit_mask = 1ULL << BOARD_BUTTON,
                             .mode = GPIO_MODE_INPUT,
                             .pull_up_en = GPIO_PULLUP_DISABLE,
                             .pull_down_en = GPIO_PULLDOWN_DISABLE,
                             .intr_type = GPIO_INTR_DISABLE,
    };

The `<<` operator in `.pin_bit_mask = 1ULL << BOARD_BUTTON` causes
astyle to treat subsequent fields as continuation lines, indenting
them to align under the operator. The i2c_bus_config initializer on
lines 24-31 is not affected because its fields have no operators.

This was introduced by commit 301b825 (ci: establish baseline firmware
formatting) and is now enforced by `just format-check`.

## Fix options
a) Wrap the expression: `.pin_bit_mask = (1ULL << BOARD_BUTTON),`
   — parentheses prevent continuation detection
b) Lower `--max-continuation-indent` in the Justfile astyle flags
   from 120 to something like 40

Suggested: (a) — minimal change, no global reformat needed.

title: firmware: mod_io_read_digital_inputs masks with MOD_IO_RELAY_MASK_ALL instead of a digital input constant
description:
## What is wrong
mod_io.c:435 masks the digital input readback with MOD_IO_RELAY_MASK_ALL:
  *out_mask = (uint8_t)(read_value & MOD_IO_RELAY_MASK_ALL);

The value 0x0F is numerically correct for 4 digital inputs, but the
constant name MOD_IO_RELAY_MASK_ALL is semantically wrong — it refers
to relays, not inputs. If relay and digital input counts ever diverge,
this would silently break.

mod_io.h defines MOD_IO_DIGITAL_INPUT_COUNT (4) but has no
corresponding MOD_IO_DIGITAL_INPUT_MASK_ALL constant.

The same issue appears in test_app/main/test_mod_io_device.c:64 which
uses MOD_IO_RELAY_MASK_ALL to validate digital input reads.

## Fix
Add to mod_io.h:
  #define MOD_IO_DIGITAL_INPUT_MASK_ALL 0x0FU
Use it in mod_io.c:435 and test_mod_io_device.c:64.
close_reason: Completed

title: QA Foundation & Test Infrastructure
description:
## QA Foundation & Test Infrastructure Epic

Master plan: docs/qa-plan.md

Comprehensive quality assurance infrastructure for the ESP32-EVB relay
controller firmware. This epic is the highest-priority prerequisite
before any remaining firmware or CLI implementation work continues.

## Scope

- Tier 1: Host unit tests (Linux, no hardware) for device_config, relay, mod_io
- Tier 2: On-device Unity tests (ESP32-EVB hardware) for all 5 components
- Tier 3: Integration/system tests (full firmware + pytest over serial/network)
- Formatting enforcement: astyle_py + pre-commit hook
- Build automation: Justfile recipes for all test/format/CI gates
- Documentation: AGENTS.md quality gate updates

## Why

The project currently has 5 custom ESP-IDF components with ZERO automated
tests. Every subsequent feature bead is riskier without regression coverage.
Auth, relay control, MOD-IO handling, and REST API behavior can ship broken
with no fast feedback loop. This epic establishes the testing foundation
that all future development depends on.

## Critical Gate

Command `0x40` relay-state readback is the authoritative MOD-IO model.
mod_io and rest_api tests should follow that behavior consistently, while
follow-up firmware work removes the older synthetic unknown-state cache
from the current component implementation.

title: On-device MOD-IO tests
description:
## What

Write on-device Unity tests for the mod_io component in
firmware/test_app/main/test_mod_io_device.c.

### Authoritative model

Command `0x40` relay-state readback is authoritative for the deployed
MOD-IO board. Device tests should verify that behavior directly.

### Test Cases (from QA plan section 2)

- I2C probe finds device at `0x58`
- Relay set + readback: write mask `0x05`, read back `0x05`
- Digital input read returns valid mask (bits `0-3` only)
- Analog input read: 4 channels return values in `0-1023` range
- All-off after test: write `0x00`; verify readback `0x00`

### Test Hygiene

Tests MUST restore MOD-IO relays to all-off (mask `0x00`) before exit.
The MOD-IO board controls real physical relays; leaving them
energized is unsafe.

## Why

Host tests verify I2C protocol bytes via stubs. Device tests verify
real I2C communication with the MOD-IO hardware at address `0x58`,
including probe, relay control, and input sampling.

## Considerations

- These tests require MOD-IO hardware physically connected to the
  ESP32-EVB via UEXT I2C (SDA=`GPIO13`, SCL=`GPIO16`)
- If MOD-IO is not connected, tests should be skippable
  (not hard-fail the entire suite)
- Analog inputs depend on what's connected to the MOD-IO
  terminals; tests should verify range (`0-1023`) not specific values

## Acceptance Criteria

- All test cases pass with MOD-IO connected at `0x58`
- Relay readback assertions follow the authoritative `0x40` model
- MOD-IO relays are all-off after test suite completes
- Tests registered in `test_app/main/test_main.c`

title: Create integration test structure with pytest fixtures
description:
## What

Create the Tier 3 integration test infrastructure at
firmware/test_integration/.

NOTE: Integration tests are INDEPENDENT of the test_app project.
They flash PRODUCTION firmware (not test_app) and exercise the
assembled system over HTTP. The only shared dependency is
pytest-embedded (installed via pip).

### Files to Create

```
firmware/test_integration/
  conftest.py              # Shared fixtures: serial provisioning,
                           # DUT discovery, HTTP client
  pytest_integration.py    # System-level pytest scenarios
```

### conftest.py Design

Shared pytest fixtures that own cross-test setup and cleanup:

**DUT discovery fixture:**
- Resolves device IP from network (mDNS or direct config)
- Provides base URL for HTTP client

**Auth provisioning fixture:**
- Establishes a known valid API token before authenticated HTTP
  checks using the same serial provisioning path the product
  already supports (scripts/provision.sh or equivalent)
- Does NOT depend on scraping a one-time random token from boot
  logs — that's fragile and timing-dependent
- Does NOT require a test-only auth bypass in production firmware
  — that would be a security hole

**HTTP client fixture:**
- Pre-configured requests session with auth headers
- Base URL from DUT discovery
- Timeout configuration

**Cleanup fixtures:**
- Relay safe state restoration after test suite
- Config restoration if tests mutated device config

### Test Architecture

Integration tests flash and drive the PRODUCTION firmware binary
(from `idf.py build` in firmware/), NOT the test_app binary. The
Justfile recipe is:

```just
test-integration:
    cd firmware && idf.py build
    cd firmware && pytest --target esp32 test_integration/ --port ...
```

This means integration tests verify the exact binary that ships to
users, not a test-specific variant.

## Why

Integration tests drive the full firmware over network. The fixtures
must handle the complexity of device discovery, authentication, and
cleanup so individual test functions stay focused on behavior
verification.

## Considerations

- Auth setup is the hardest fixture: it must work deterministically
  without test-only firmware code or fragile log scraping
- The serial provisioning approach (set token via serial) is the
  same path operators use, so testing it is itself valuable
- Fixtures should own cleanup so a failure in one test doesn't
  poison later tests
- This scaffold has NO dependency on test_app — the two test
  projects are completely independent

## Acceptance Criteria

- conftest.py provides working DUT, auth, and HTTP client fixtures
- Fixtures handle cleanup on test failure (no leaked relay states)
- Auth provisioning uses serial path, not log scraping or bypass
- pytest discovers the integration test directory correctly

title: Integration tests for REST API end-to-end scenarios
description:
## What

Write system-level integration tests in
firmware/test_integration/pytest_integration.py that exercise the
full firmware stack over HTTP.

### Test Cases (from QA plan section 2)

**Status endpoint:**
- GET /api/v1/status returns valid JSON with expected schema

**Relay control:**
- Relay state changes via REST API propagate to actual relay state

**Auth enforcement:**
- Requests without token -> 401
- Requests with valid token -> 200

**Invalid token path:**
- Returns the documented auth error (401 or 403, whichever
  contract the firmware adopts)
- Does NOT expose device-context headers (X-FW-Version,
  X-ModIO-Present, X-ModIO-Sync) on pre-auth error responses

**Authenticated response headers:**
- Authenticated responses include device-context headers
- Pre-auth 401/403 responses do NOT include device-context headers

### Test Architecture

These tests run against the PRODUCTION firmware (not test_app).
The flow is:
1. idf.py build (production firmware)
2. Flash production firmware to device
3. Provision auth token via serial
4. Run HTTP-based test scenarios from the host

### Why Integration Tests

Tier 1 and Tier 2 tests verify components in isolation. Integration
tests verify the assembled system: that REST API handlers correctly
call relay/mod_io/device_config components, that auth middleware
gates access properly, and that response headers carry the right
device context.

## Considerations

- Tests require both serial access (for provisioning) and network
  access (for HTTP) to the ESP32-EVB
- The device must have working Ethernet with a DHCP-assigned IP
  reachable from the test host
- Tests should be idempotent — each test leaves the device in a
  known state
- Auth header tests are security-relevant: they verify the
  information leakage boundary between authenticated and
  unauthenticated contexts

## Acceptance Criteria

- All test cases pass against production firmware on ESP32-EVB
- Auth boundary tests verify header presence/absence correctly
- Tests clean up relay state after execution
- No dependency on test-only firmware code or auth bypass

title: Create Justfile with all QA recipes
description:
## What

Create a Justfile at the project root with all build, test, format,
and CI recipes as specified in QA plan section 5.

### Recipes

| Recipe              | What                                        |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| just build          | idf.py build (ESP32 target)                 |
| just test           | cmake + ctest host tests (Tier 1)           |
| just test-device    | idf.py build + pytest-embedded test_app     |
| just test-integration | idf.py build + pytest-embedded integration|
| just format         | astyle_py auto-fix                          |
| just format-check   | astyle_py dry-run (CI gate)                 |
| just ci             | format-check + build + test                 |
| just ci-full        | ci + test-device + test-integration         |
| just setup          | install QA deps + pre-commit hook           |
| just clean          | rm build artifacts                          |

### Configuration Variables

```just
serial_port := env("EVB_SERIAL_PORT", "/dev/ttyS4")
test_app_sdkconfig_defaults := env("EVB_TEST_APP_SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS",
                                   "sdkconfig.defaults")
```

### Key Design Points

- All idf.py, pytest-embedded, and Unity invocations assume the
  ESP-IDF environment is already active in the current shell
- Hardware recipes (test-device, test-integration) combine build
  and pytest in one recipe because pytest-embedded needs a built app
- format and format-check use rg --files to find C/H files while
  excluding build/, managed_components/, and test build directories
- ci recipe chains: format-check + build + test (fast gate)
- ci-full adds hardware tests on top of ci (self-hosted runner)
- For CI hardware lanes, set EVB_TEST_APP_SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS to
  layer sdkconfig.ci on top of sdkconfig.defaults

### Exact Recipes

See QA plan section 5 for the complete recipe definitions including
astyle_py flags, cmake invocations, and pytest arguments.

## Why

The Justfile provides a single entry point for all QA operations.
Agents and developers run `just ci` before committing. CI runs
`just ci-full` on the self-hosted runner. No need to remember
individual tool invocations.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Create pre-commit hook for formatting enforcement
description:
## What

Create tools/pre-commit-hook.sh — a shell script that checks the
staged snapshot of firmware/**/*.{c,h} files against astyle_py.

### Design

Same AStyle flags as just format-check, but only operates on staged
files for speed and correctness with partial staging. The hook:

1. Collects staged C/H files via git diff --cached --name-only
2. Filters to firmware/**/*.{c,h}, excluding build/ and
   managed_components/ directories
3. Exits 0 if no staged C/H files
4. Checks astyle_py availability, fails with install hint if missing
5. Extracts staged content to a temp directory (handles partial
   staging correctly by using git show :path)
6. Runs astyle_py --dry-run on the staged versions
7. Reports formatting errors with "Run just format to fix" hint

### AStyle Flags (must match just format exactly)

--astyle-version=3.4.7 --style=otbs --attach-namespaces
--attach-classes --indent=spaces=4 --convert-tabs
--align-reference=name --keep-one-line-statements --pad-header
--pad-oper --unpad-paren --max-continuation-indent=120

### Installation

The just setup recipe copies this script to .git/hooks/pre-commit
and makes it executable.

### ORDERING CONSTRAINT

The format baseline pass (evb-2ee.18) MUST be committed BEFORE this
hook is installed via `just setup`. Otherwise, existing unformatted
code will fail the hook on the next commit. The verification gate
(evb-2ee.21) ensures correct ordering by depending on both beads,
but agents should be aware: do NOT run `just setup` until the
baseline formatting commit has landed.

Sequence: (1) run baseline format → (2) commit formatted code →
(3) create hook script → (4) run `just setup` to install hook.

## Why

The pre-commit hook catches formatting violations before they enter
the repository. Without it, agents and developers can commit
unformatted code that breaks just format-check in CI. The hook is
the first line of defense.

## Considerations

- The hook checks STAGED content, not working tree content. This
  means partial staging (git add -p) is handled correctly.
- Extracting staged content to a temp dir avoids modifying the
  working tree during the hook
- The hook must use the same flags as just format-check or
  developers get inconsistent results
- Agents should be able to run just format before committing to
  auto-fix any violations

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hook blocks commits with C/H formatting violations
- Hook passes when code is properly formatted
- Hook only checks staged firmware C/H files (ignores non-firmware)
- Hook handles partial staging correctly
- just setup installs the hook
close_reason: Added staged-snapshot formatting hook and wired just setup to install it
